chunks: And he (peace be upon him) said: O son of Adam,

livelihood is of two kinds: the livelihood which you seek and the livelihood which seeks you; if you do not reach it, it will come to you. Therefore, do not turn your one day’s worry into a year’s worry. Whatever you get every day should be enough for you for the day. If you have a whole year of your life even then Allāh, the Sublime, will give you every next day what He has destined as your share. If you do not have a year in your life then why should you worry for what is not for you. No seeker will reach your livelihood before you nor will anyone overpower you in the matter of livelihood. Similarly, whatever has been destined as your share will not be delayed for you.
ai.seo_question: What is the Islamic perspective on anxiety about future sustenance and divine decree?
ai.summary: In this famous hadith from Nahj al-Balagha, Imam Ali (AS) distinguishes between 'rizq al-talab' (sustenance sought through effort) and 'rizq al-talabuka' (sustenance that comes independently), using this duality to alleviate the anxiety of over-planning. This teaching underscores the Shia concept of balancing human agency (kasb) with divine decree (qadr), reassuring believers that their destined provision cannot be outpaced by others or delayed by time. It serves as a practical spiritual remedy for 'hamm' (worry), encouraging trust in Allah's daily sustenance rather than hoarding mental energy for uncertain futures.
